description:
Your ledger is a plain-text file. You own it for good.

Beancount brings serious double-entry bookkeeping to your phone without locking your financial history inside a proprietary database. Record a purchase in seconds, inspect the underlying Beancount file, and keep a Git history of every change.

FINANCIAL CLARITY
• See net worth, assets, liabilities, income, and expenses
• Compare spending across months, quarters, and years
• Explore cash flow, profit trends, budgets, merchants, and account reports

YOUR BOOKS, YOUR FORMAT
• Keep real Beancount-syntax text files
• Browse commits, authors, and line-by-line changes
• Edit the ledger source directly and take your files with you

BUILT FOR REAL BOOKS
• Full double-entry transactions, splits, transfers, and reimbursements
• Multiple ledgers, currencies, investments, crypto, and property
• Receipt capture, payee and account suggestions, search, and filters

Beancount is free, with no ads and no in-app purchases.
promotionalText: See your whole financial life, keep the plain-text ledger, and understand every change through Git history and full reports.
whatsNew:
Home and Accounts now value investments at market price. The line under a total says when a price is stale or a holding is counted at cost; tap it on Home to see each holding’s price date. Net Worth shows cost and unrealized gain, a single fund reads in its own units with its cost beneath, and a balance that cannot be converted is named instead of silently dropped.

Budgets are measured over the same days as your spending, so year to date and the current month no longer compare against a whole period. Transfers between your own accounts show the amount moved instead of zero, and negative amounts keep their minus sign.

Counts read naturally in every language, the date picker follows your language, and payee and narration fields no longer autocorrect. New Transaction asks before discarding a draft, and a transaction changed elsewhere offers a reload instead of an error.

Larger text sizes keep transaction rows, sign-in buttons, and amounts readable, and screen readers announce the selected option in pickers.
